# Diagnostics and Triage
## Handheld analyzer
1. Hold the [color=#58e6d9]HandheldHealthAnalyzer[/color]. 2. Use it on the patient. 3. Read the medical diagnostics window.
The handheld analyzer reports approximate oxygenation, circulating blood, perfusion, pressure, rhythm, pain, shock, consciousness, external bleeding, and observable regional injury signs.
## Full body scan
1. Place and buckle the patient into a [color=#58e6d9]MedicalScanner[/color]. 2. Open the nearby [color=#58e6d9]computerBodyScanner[/color] console. 3. Select medical diagnostics.
The scanner reports exact wounds, internal bleeding, fractures, structural damage, organ function, drugs, cyberware, and active surgical sites.
## Interface sections
- [color=#58e6d9]Priority triage feed[/color] — active threats ordered by urgency. - [color=#58e6d9]Vital telemetry[/color] — oxygenation, blood, perfusion, pressure, rhythm, pain, and shock. - [color=#58e6d9]Regions[/color] — injury burden and function of body regions. - [color=#58e6d9]Wounds[/color] — type, severity, bleeding, contamination, infection, and applied treatment. - [color=#58e6d9]Organs[/color] — internal organ integrity and function. - [color=#58e6d9]Cyberware[/color] — integrity, power, heat, EMP state, and neural link. - [color=#58e6d9]Drugs[/color] — concentration, therapeutic effects, and toxic burden.
## Triage priority
1. Massive or arterial external bleeding. 2. Absent breathing or circulation, or critical hypoxia. 3. Internal bleeding, vital organ damage, or critical shock. 4. Open fracture, tendon rupture, nerve damage, or vascular injury. 5. Stable wounds, infection, pain, and scheduled surgery.
Repeat the scan after treatment and verify that the medical revision and affected values changed.
